findings.claim: Bulk purge (purge_all_trash, and each batch of purge_all_missing) still calls the strict physical_delete in a loop with a single commit after the loop, so a 409 on a later ambiguous file leaves earlier files unlinked on disk while their row deletions roll back.
findings.impact: After one ambiguous entry, Trash or Missing rows remain for files already removed from disk, until the user purges again; the second purge succeeds because the unlink is skipped for an absent file. No data beyond the already-purged files is lost.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/fileops.py:756-759 (loop of physical_delete, then one db.commit) and :811-814 (per-batch commit); physical_delete at :670 raises through existing_or_409 before the unlink at :673. No fix commit since the previous review touched this.

bucket_proposal.reason: I12 requires 409 and no change for the ambiguous file itself; it does not define the partial state of a batch. Recoverable by repeating the purge.

findings.proposed_fix: Catch the 409 per file in the bulk loops and skip that file, or commit per row.

findings.claim: The new parity table covers only the non-strict resolver: it has no case for several matching entries, the sorted-bytes tie rule, an empty or absolute component, or an unreadable directory.
findings.impact: Addon resolver copies could diverge from core on ambiguity or empty-component handling while still passing the table, so I16 gives less protection than its wording suggests.
findings.evidence: backend/tests/fixtures/diskpath_parity.json lists 8 cases (exact, nfd leaf/ancestor/both, twin, nothing, real ancestor, dot-dot) and backend/tests/test_diskpath_parity.py calls only resolve_on_disk with strict off.

bucket_proposal.reason: I16 is met for the inputs the table holds; the gap is in what it holds, not a broken invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: Add cases for the sorted-bytes tie and empty components.

specification_compliance: I16 core copy: the parity fixture and a table-driven test now exist (commit 675fa188), which answers the earlier finding that none existed. Addon copies are not in this commit.
I3/I4/I12: _walk checks the exact name first, treats empty, '.' and '..' as matching nothing, falls back to an NFC-equal scandir match and writes nothing.
I5-I8, I12: mutators use existing_or_409 and new_or_409 and never the cache; name_taken covers the other spelling.
I11: the cache hit is confirmed by lexists and dropped otherwise; mutators skip it.
I13: the AST inventory test has a seeded-detector self-check; LISTING_DERIVED is empty.
I14, I15: addon work, out of this commit.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Several handlers (folder operations, batch_move, batch_rename, rename/move, complete_upload, empty_trash, purge_all_missing) now run in worker threads with the request Session.
start_import is split into prepare_import and launch_import, with prepare_import run in a worker thread.
physical_delete can now raise 409 partway through a bulk purge.
regression_risks: Cross-thread use of the request SQLAlchemy Session in the to_thread handlers; calls are sequential per request, so I saw no concrete race.
markdown_image_import module globals (_jobs, _current_job_id) are mutated from a worker thread in prepare_import.
Mutators refuse an ambiguous pair while readers pick the first by sorted bytes.
One extra lexists per resolve and a scandir per unresolved component on hot read paths.
test_coverage: Strong HTTP coverage of I1-I12 over leaf, ancestor and both layouts, including 409 on ambiguity, failed batch rename rollback, scan stability and symlink rejection.
The parity test now runs 8 table cases against the core resolver.
No test covers a bulk purge that meets an ambiguous entry, the complete_upload leaf resolve, or the thread offloading.
The inventory detector depends on the DRIVE_PART name regex, so a join with an unusual variable name can be missed.
not_verified: I ran no tests; the tools are read-only.
I did not check SQLAlchemy Session thread-safety under asyncio.to_thread.
I did not read the main.py purge job exception handling or the scanner change in full.
I did not inspect the addon repositories or compare resolver copies.
I did not check whether the inventory regex misses real joins.
trajectory: The two fix commits since the previous review do not patch the design. The first adds the parity JSON fixture and a table-driven test, which only adds test coverage and no new branch, state or prediction in the resolver. The second records the review in docs. No round added a branch, state or prediction that an earlier round also added, and no round removed one.
